items.title: Shared document authority names its principal consumers
items.statement: The core explicitly assigns document panes, editor tabs, chat virtual documents, restore/reload, revert, pending-sync state, URI identity, and post-save didSave emission to the LspSupervisor plus DocumentStore authority boundary, so those principal consumers are not left unnamed.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LspSupervisor plus DocumentStore is the authority boundary for document panes, editor tabs, chat virtual documents, restore/reload, revert, pending-sync state, virtual/real URI identity, and didSave emission after successful shared-store save.

items.title: DocumentStore transition and transaction semantics are absent
items.statement: The authority is named, but the core does not define legal pending-sync, reload, restore, revert, and save transitions; conflict arbitration between concurrent panes; atomic commit boundaries; or rollback behavior after a shared-store write partly succeeds. Implementations can therefore disagree about which buffer and state win after races or partial failure.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LspSupervisor plus DocumentStore is the authority boundary for document panes, editor tabs, chat virtual documents, restore/reload, revert, pending-sync state, virtual/real URI identity, and didSave emission after successful shared-store save.
- LSP never reads a second document authority for an open file.

items.impact: Races or partial store failures can leave the editor, protocol peer, and persistence layer with different document truth.
items.builder_discretion: Specify the state machine, serialized mutation boundary, conflict policy, and compensating or retry behavior without introducing a second authority.

items.title: Protocol I/O is explicitly excluded from the UI thread
items.statement: The core explicitly requires asynchronous protocol I/O and Slint event-loop dispatch, including a direct prohibition on blocking the UI.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LSP message flow covers open, edit, diagnostics, hover, and completion while keeping all protocol I/O on async tasks and routing UI updates through the Slint event loop rather than blocking the interface.
- UI must never block on LSP protocol I/O.

items.title: Async task cancellation, backpressure, and dispatch failure are unspecified
items.statement: Moving protocol work to async tasks avoids UI blocking but does not define cancellation ownership, queue bounds, overload behavior, shutdown draining, error propagation, or what happens when the target UI object can no longer be upgraded. These omissions leave race, leak, and stale-update behavior builder-defined.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LSP message flow covers open, edit, diagnostics, hover, and completion while keeping all protocol I/O on async tasks and routing UI updates through the Slint event loop rather than blocking the interface.
- Weak::upgrade_in_event_loop

items.impact: Large or abandoned request streams can consume unbounded resources or deliver updates after their UI consumer is gone.
items.builder_discretion: Define bounded queues, cancellation tokens and owners, shutdown semantics, dispatch-failure handling, and user-visible error propagation.

items.title: Stale response identity and UI suppression are explicit
items.statement: The core identifies session epoch, URI, document version, request generation, and request class as freshness inputs, and explicitly forbids stale responses from updating UI, applying completion, navigating, or triggering automatic re-request.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Document-scoped LSP responses carry enough identity to discard stale or superseded replies by session epoch, URI, document version, request generation, and request class; discarded UX replies remain trace-visible and are not automatically re-requested.
- Stale document-scoped responses must not update UI, apply completion, navigate, or auto re-request.

items.title: Trace lifecycle, redaction, and operator recovery are undefined
items.statement: Discarded replies remain trace-visible, but the core does not define log retention, size limits, access authority, URI or request-data redaction, correlation fields beyond request id, or an operator and user recovery path when a reply is discarded and automatic re-request is prohibited.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Document-scoped LSP responses carry enough identity to discard stale or superseded replies by session epoch, URI, document version, request generation, and request class; discarded UX replies remain trace-visible and are not automatically re-requested.
- trace `/logs`

items.impact: Sensitive document identity may persist without policy, while users and support staff lack a deterministic way to recover from discarded work requests.
items.builder_discretion: Define safe trace fields, redaction, access, retention and rotation, correlation, and a bounded manual retry or refresh affordance.

items.title: URI identity and position conversion are centralized
items.statement: The core establishes one canonical DocumentUri, one position-mapping layer, explicit one-based and zero-based boundaries, negotiated encoding with a UTF-16 baseline, and a prohibition on handler-local code-unit math and duplicate physical-file identities.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Document identity, freshness, and position conversion use one canonical DocumentUri per document and host, a centralized position-mapping layer, UI 1-based and LSP 0-based boundaries, negotiated position encoding with UTF-16 baseline, and no handler-local code-unit math.
- The same physical file must not gain duplicate identities through case, slash, drive-letter, URI spelling, session/URI pairing, or path/position conversion differences.

items.title: Malformed URI and encoding-negotiation failure policy is missing
items.statement: The core names common identity differences and a UTF-16 baseline but does not specify rejection and normalization for malformed or adversarial URIs, percent encoding, dot segments, symlinks, UNC or remote schemes, Unicode normalization, or invalid and unsupported server position-encoding advertisements. It also lacks a defined fail-closed fallback when conversion cannot be proven exact.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Document identity, freshness, and position conversion use one canonical DocumentUri per document and host, a centralized position-mapping layer, UI 1-based and LSP 0-based boundaries, negotiated position encoding with UTF-16 baseline, and no handler-local code-unit math.
- The same physical file must not gain duplicate identities through case, slash, drive-letter, URI spelling, session/URI pairing, or path/position conversion differences.

items.impact: A crafted or unusual URI or encoding advertisement can alias documents, escape an authority boundary, or place edits and diagnostics at the wrong offsets.
items.builder_discretion: Define accepted schemes and hosts, canonicalization and rejection rules, platform-specific alias handling, negotiation validation, and safe conversion-failure behavior.

items.title: FIFO, barriers, rebase, and failed-save UI truth are explicit
items.statement: The core explicitly requires per-session FIFO sync, Ready and sync barriers, newest-only soft requests, debounce coalescing, rebase by whole-document replacement or restart, and suppression of didSave and synchronized UI truth after a failed save.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Sync ordering is FIFO per session, document-scoped requests wait for Ready and sync barriers, soft requests keep only the newest request class, didChange debounce coalesces mutations, whole-document replacement or restart rebases when incremental confidence is lost, and failed saves do not emit didSave or imply synchronization.
- Failed save does not emit didSave and stale-result handling must not make the UI look saved or synchronized.

items.title: Queue limits and network-loss recovery are undefined
items.statement: FIFO, barriers, coalescing, and restart are named, but the core does not define queue capacities, barrier timeouts, overflow policy, cancellation across a restart, replay after transport loss, reconnect backoff, deduplication of uncertainly delivered changes, or the user-visible state while offline. The rebase trigger and completion oracle are also unspecified.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Sync ordering is FIFO per session, document-scoped requests wait for Ready and sync barriers, soft requests keep only the newest request class, didChange debounce coalesces mutations, whole-document replacement or restart rebases when incremental confidence is lost, and failed saves do not emit didSave or imply synchronization.

items.impact: Sustained edits or a disconnect can create unbounded memory use, indefinite waits, duplicated change delivery, or silent divergence after restart.
items.builder_discretion: Specify bounds, overflow and timeout behavior, connection states, retry and backoff, replay or full-resync rules, cancellation boundaries, and observable recovery completion.

items.title: Legacy alias conflict precedence and migration lifecycle are missing
items.statement: Read/write mapping of the legacy disabled key is required, but the core does not say which value wins when canonical and legacy keys coexist, whether writes mirror or remove the alias, how conflicts are surfaced, when the alias can be retired, or how downgrade compatibility is preserved.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LSP config uses lsp.enabled and lsp.servers.<id>.* keys for disable, command, extensions, env, and initialization while supporting lsp.<id>.disabled as a read/write compatibility alias aligned with OpenCode schema.
- The legacy alias must map to the canonical lsp.servers.<id>.disabled namespace rather than creating a second config family.

items.impact: Conflicting keys can make enablement differ across readers and writes, and upgrades or downgrades can silently change server state.
items.builder_discretion: Define deterministic precedence, conflict reporting, write normalization, versioned migration, rollback, and retirement criteria.

items.title: Project config can influence command and environment without a trust boundary
items.statement: The combined units allow command and environment configuration and project-level overrides, but do not define precedence between app and project values, schema validation, allowed command and environment fields, project trust or consent, secret handling, file permissions, atomic persistence, or protection against an untrusted workspace causing process execution under user authority.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LSP config uses lsp.enabled and lsp.servers.<id>.* keys for disable, command, extensions, env, and initialization while supporting lsp.<id>.disabled as a read/write compatibility alias aligned with OpenCode schema.

canonical_text: LSP configuration stores app-level and optional project-level overrides with debounced change, hover, completion, workspace symbol, and hover-delay timeout controls documented in Settings or developer-facing implementation guidance.

items.impact: An untrusted project or weakly protected local file could alter executable command or environment configuration, expose secrets, or produce non-deterministic effective settings.
items.builder_discretion: Define trust and consent, override precedence, validation and allowlists, secret redaction and storage, permissions, atomic writes, and safe failure behavior.

items.title: Settings accessibility, localization, and complete range rules are absent
items.statement: The core identifies a Settings destination and some defaults and ranges, but does not define labels and descriptions for localization, keyboard and assistive-technology operation, validation announcements, reduced-motion considerations for status changes, or valid ranges and invalid-value fallback for every timeout.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LSP configuration stores app-level and optional project-level overrides with debounced change, hover, completion, workspace symbol, and hover-delay timeout controls documented in Settings or developer-facing implementation guidance.
- Settings → Editor or Developer
- Timeout and debounce defaults must remain user-configurable.

items.impact: Users can receive inaccessible or untranslated controls and inconsistent behavior for missing, malformed, or out-of-range timeout values.
items.builder_discretion: Define localized copy keys, accessible names and error announcements, keyboard behavior, every value domain, and deterministic invalid-value fallback.

items.title: Revert lacks destructive-action safeguards
items.statement: Revert is placed under the shared authority but the core does not specify unsaved-change detection, confirmation, snapshot or undo, scope when multiple panes share a buffer, cancellation, or recovery after a revert fails midway.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LspSupervisor plus DocumentStore is the authority boundary for document panes, editor tabs, chat virtual documents, restore/reload, revert, pending-sync state, virtual/real URI identity, and didSave emission after successful shared-store save.
- /revert

items.impact: A revert can silently destroy shared unsaved work or leave consumers on different versions.
items.builder_discretion: Define confirmation and authority rules, recoverable snapshots or undo, multi-consumer scope, and atomic failure behavior.

items.title: Cross-unit dependency graph is empty despite runtime ordering seams
items.statement: The core preserves owner references, but every shown unit has an empty depends_on array even though async responses, freshness identity, URI mapping, sync barriers, shared-store save truth, and configuration jointly constrain the same pipeline. The absent dependency edges leave construction and validation order ambiguous across owner documents and units.

items.impact: Builders can implement or validate downstream behavior before required authority, identity, synchronization, and configuration contracts exist.
items.builder_discretion: Add explicit dependency and consumer edges or a shared integration contract with ordering and conformance responsibilities.

items.title: Acceptance surfaces do not falsify runtime behavior
items.statement: The acceptance criteria and validation surfaces verify source preservation, addressing, indexing, and migration structure, but provide no executable oracles for authority races, stale-response suppression, position conversion, sync barriers, failed saves, alias precedence, timeout behavior, offline recovery, or security boundaries.

items.builder_discretion: Add deterministic unit, integration, race, property, fault-injection, migration, accessibility, and security acceptance oracles tied to each contract.

items.title: Host and transport diversity remains an explicit review unknown
items.statement: Within this blind window it is unknown whether other canonical owners define remote hosts, virtualized filesystems, multiple LSP transports, process sandboxing, or platform-specific path and case behavior. The local owner-boundary note delegates some truth but does not identify which referenced owner supplies these contracts.

- Plans/LSPSupport.md owns LSP-specific protocol/client constraints while referenced owner docs retain their SSOT boundaries.

items.impact: Unseen owner contracts may close these risks, but this unit cannot be implemented safely if they do not.
items.builder_discretion: Resolve the named owner seams before implementation and convert each unknown into an explicit contract or a documented non-applicability decision.

dimension_assessments.summary: LSPS-048 explicitly names the principal document consumers and operations governed by the shared authority.
Pending-sync, reload, restore, revert, save, reconnect, and rebase state transitions and invalid-transition handling are not defined.
FIFO and stale suppression close some races, but shared-store arbitration, async lifecycle, queueing, restart, and UI-target teardown races remain unspecified.
Failed save truth is explicit, but partial shared-store writes, UI dispatch failure, uncertain transport delivery, and config persistence failure lack contracts.
Whole-document replacement or restart is named, but completion, retry, rollback, revert recovery, and uncertain-delivery handling are absent.
The document authority is explicit, while project configuration authority over command and environment values and cross-owner responsibilities remain undefined.
Trace retention and redaction plus configuration secret storage, permissions, and lifecycle are not specified.
Malformed URIs and encoding advertisements and untrusted project command, environment, and timeout values lack complete validation and trust rules.
Stale replies are forbidden from updating the UI and failed saves are forbidden from appearing saved or synchronized.
Disconnect detection, offline state, reconnect backoff, replay, deduplication, and recovery completion are absent.
Async, sync, trace, and configuration flows do not specify queue, document, log, or cardinality bounds and overload behavior.
Settings and failure-status interactions lack keyboard, accessible-name, and error-announcement requirements.
Settings destination and controls are named without localized copy, formatting, or fallback requirements.
A legacy read/write alias exists, but conflict precedence, normalization, migration, downgrade, and retirement rules are absent.
Stale replies remain trace-visible, but safe fields, correlation, retention, rotation, access, recovery guidance, and broader failure events are unspecified.
Revert is named without confirmation, shared-buffer scope, recoverable snapshot, cancellation, or atomic failure behavior.
Owner boundaries are acknowledged, but dependency edges and conformance responsibilities across the document, LSP, GUI, storage, and GitHub owners are missing.
The listed acceptance and validation surfaces check planning structure rather than executable runtime outcomes and failure cases.
Remote hosts, transport diversity, process sandboxing, and platform-specific identity rules may exist in unseen owners but cannot be established from this blind window.
